label: Prairie / wildflower meadow
plain: A mostly native open area with grasses and wildflowers.
simple_note: Best choice for restored Blackland Prairie, no-mow native meadows, and seeded conservation areas.

label: Wetland / pond edge
plain: A soggy or seasonally wet place that slows water and supports wetland plants.
simple_note: Use only where the site really has wetland or wet-soil function.

label: Woodland / forest
plain: An upland area mostly covered by trees.
simple_note: Useful for wooded areas, but this is a national fallback value.

label: Creekside woods
plain: Trees along a creek, drainage, river, or floodplain.
simple_note: Use only for wooded creek corridors or floodplain forest.

label: Mostly non-native grass
plain: A grassy area dominated by introduced or exotic grasses.
simple_note: Best available Texas value for non-native grass cover.

label: Mowed turf field
plain: A regularly mowed lawn, field, or turf area.
simple_note: No clean Central Texas turf ecosystem-service value was found. This starting estimate uses the non-native grass value and can be changed if the user has better local data.

label: Other open green land
plain: A vegetated open area that is not clearly prairie, wetland, forest, or turf.
simple_note: Fallback class only. Pick a more specific category when possible.

label: Urban green open space
simple_note: Broad category with overlap risk. Not recommended as the default for prairie restoration.
